alyssa: CI went red on master, intermittent failure in test_retry_backoff::jitter_variation under `--jobs=8`. Failing ~1/8 runs on linux-x86. Anyone seen this before?
ron: saw a similar one yesterday when I ran the suite in the docker harness. Assertion is `backoff decreased: prev=57ms now=12ms` from runtime/src/retry/mod.rs:213. Looks like timers are observed out-of-order under load.
ci-bot: buildkite #8672 — step "unit-tests (linux-x86)" failed (exit 1): https://buildkite.com/redwood/builds/8672
sam: can you paste the exact assert and a short snippet of surrounding log? If we can repro deterministically we can bisect.
alyssa: pasted the CI snippet: ```thread 'test_retry_backoff::jitter_variation' panicked at 'backoff decreased: prev=57ms now=12ms', runtime/src/retry/mod.rs:213```
nidhi: fwiw we've hit ordering issues when the test assumes monotonic-per-request timestamps but the host scheduler and container cgroups preempt threads; clock reads can appear non-monotonic across cores. CPUfreq scaling and vDSO resolution occasionally cause this.
ron: this only triggers with `--jobs=8` and inside container for me. Quick experiments: try `RUST_TEST_THREADS=1`, set TEST_FORCE_MONOTONIC=1, or run with `--test-threads=1` to see if it's concurrency.
alyssa: kicked a rerun with pinned seed and TEST_FORCE_MONOTONIC. buildkite triggered: https://buildkite.com/redwood/builds/8673
buildkite: buildkite #8673 started (rerun of #8672)
sam: if rerun repros, collect `strace -T -f` or `perf record -e cpu-clock` around the failing process; may show time syscalls and scheduling gaps.
alyssa: rerun failed again intermittently. Short extract from the test log showing times: ```[2026-03-17T15:02:31Z] prev_backoff_ms=57 now_backoff_ms=12 seed=22458912
[2026-03-17T15:02:31Z] worker=6 pid=4321 get_time_ns=161234567890
[2026-03-17T15:02:31Z] worker=2 pid=4317 get_time_ns=161234567892```
nidhi: ns values are effectively the same but ordering flips due to scheduling; test's strict decreasing assert is brittle.
ron: short fix: relax the test assert to allow non-decreasing within a small epsilon (e.g., 1ms) or compare against a per-worker monotonic counter. Long-term: inject a TestClock trait and use a fake clock under tests.
sam: agree on TestClock for robustness. For now a small PR to relax tolerance and a TODO for TestClock sounds good. Also add an integration CI job that runs the retry tests with `--jobs=8` to catch this sooner.
alyssa: I'll open a tiny PR to change the assert to `now >= prev || (prev - now) < 2ms` and add a comment referencing this thread. PR ~30m. Ping me for review.
ron: I'll take a bisect if this resurfaces. Also happy to add the extra CI job.
nidhi: +1 for CI job and a deterministic-timers env in nightly.
ci-bot: alyssa pushed branch `fix/retry-timer-tolerance` — build triggered #8674
alyssa: thanks all, linking PR when it's up. If the fix doesn't eliminate flakes we'll follow up with the TestClock refactor and a clearer harness for timer-dependent tests.
sam: :thumbsup: if anyone notices similar timing brittleness in other modules drop a note here so we can identify a pattern.
buildkite: buildkite #8674 started (branch fix/retry-timer-tolerance)
